about: Questions for the real-world held-out set (docs/PROTOCOL.md section 3). Each workbook is either a hand-written list of questions or a `table` rule. Ground truth is never typed: external/realworld.py computes it from the workbook (cached value for lookup, the cell itself for address, the formula's direct precedents for trace, a LibreOffice recalculation of the perturbed workbook for impact). `key` makes the builder check that the described row/cell is the only match, and `labels` lists the cells a reviewer reads to check the question text against the sheet (printed in review.md).
selection_rule: Workbooks: every open-licence file in tests/real/ that holds a data table or formulas and encodes to under 150,000 tokens, plus the four native-.xlsx Damodaran models whose SHA-256 is pinned in tests/real/manifest.json. Chosen before any model run, from the sizes and formula counts in real-workbooks/MANIFEST.md. Table workbooks (`table`): rows at 20%, 50% and 80% of the data rows, the key column must identify the row uniquely, 2 lookups on the first two `lookups` columns, 1 address on `address`. Hand-written workbooks: 4-6 questions chosen for a spread of question types and layouts (label and value in separate regions, year headers in a row above, suppressed and footnoted values, a repeated label such as 'Services').
